I read the whole file: the three theorems finite_field_valued_fiber, locallyQuasiFinite_of_finite_geometric_point_fibers and locallyQuasiFinite_iff_finite_geometric_point_fibers. I did not open the Mathlib sources.

The only overlap between the two main proofs is the correspondence between lifts q with q ≫ f = g and sections of Limits.pullback.snd f g. The forward proof uses the map q ↦ lift q (via pullback.lift) and shows it is injective with pullback.lift_fst. The converse proof uses the inverse direction, s ↦ s ≫ pullback.fst, and shows it is injective with pullback.hom_ext. Each use is a few lines of universal-property bookkeeping that finishes in a different place.

The first proof ends with an algebra-homomorphism injectivity argument. The second ends with a Jacobson-space and finiteness argument. Neither contains a long block that repeats in the other. A shared equivalence lemma between lifts and sections would barely shorten either proof, so it falls under the rubric's exclusion for short calculations and thin wrappers. The iff theorem only dispatches to the other two theorems.
